text: uh before i hit this button is there an undo on it in the event its wrong
resolution: User asked, before pressing the new solidify button, whether it can be undone if the result is wrong. Answered as a how-to/safety clarification — no code changed. Verified the undo path in source: the solidify button calls props.onEditMesh, which routes to studioModel.updatePartMesh, which calls commit({kind:'partMeshUpdated'}, 'mesh', 'record') — the 'record' mode pushes the edit onto the undoable branch history as a single step. Confirmed via the existing model.undo/redo wiring (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z plus the on-screen ↶ Undo / ↷ Redo buttons top-left of the viewport) and the branch/twig law (mesh edits are BRANCH = persisted V20 + undoable). Told the user solidify is one undoable commit (one Ctrl+Z reverts the whole op cleanly, not face-by-face) and is branch-persisted so it survives hot reload. Safe to press.
